q: How do we estimate a motor's electricity use from its horsepower rating?
title: Motor horsepower to kWh
short: Convert horsepower to kilowatts (1 hp is 0.746 kW), multiply by how loaded the motor runs, divide by its efficiency, then multiply by running hours. It is an estimate; a meter or the electricity bill beats it. Use it to split a bill between machines, not to replace the bill.

ul: Nameplate rating in hp or kW (this is output power).
Typical load as a share of rating.

p: To allocate a known bill across machines or to size a saving. Your reported Scope 2 still comes from the bill.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site, and labels estimates as estimates.

example.title: Worked example (illustrative)
lines: At 75% load and 90% efficiency: 11.19 × 0.75 ÷ 0.90 = 9.33 kW input
